Also called the electric bass guitar, electric bass or simply bass, it is the lowest member of the guitar family; its construction is close to the electric guitar's, but the neck and scale length are longer. Four strings are usual, with five-, six-, seven-, eight- and twelve-string models also made; it is played with the fingers, the thumb or a pick, and because its acoustic volume is small it needs pickups and external equipment to be amplified. Its H-S number is 513. Since the 1950s it has been used mostly in popular music, displacing the double bass, and in rock, heavy metal, blues, jazz, Latin, funk and other styles it takes the bass part or solos; in a modern rock band it is played by the bassist.
貝斯吉他屬吉他家族最低音者，四弦通常調為E、A、D、G，比吉他最低四弦低八度；五: The bass guitar is the lowest instrument of the guitar family; the four strings are usually tuned E, A, D, G, an octave below the guitar's lowest four. Five-string models usually add a low B and six-string models a high C. The instrument itself is quiet, and its volume has to be controlled through an external amplifier or monitoring equipment; electromagnetic or piezoelectric pickups turn the vibration of the strings into an electrical signal, and the way the strings are wound also affects the sound. A long scale length helps the low B resonate. Compared with the guitar it has a longer neck and scale length and a lower range; compared with the double bass it feeds back less readily when amplified through pickups, and the frets make intonation easier to control.

In the band it mainly provides the bass and the rhythm, and it also solos in jazz, fusion, Latin, funk and some rock songs.
